title: Adaptive prioritization for private/VPC requests by data sensitivity and network maturity
creator: Morgan Lee
description: Problem: We receive a steady stream of private/VPC/on-prem deployment requests that vary widely in their urgency and technical runway. Current intake often treats similar requests the same, resulting in overloaded engineering schedules for low-risk customers and slow turnaround for high-risk, high-impact requests. Goal: Define and operationalize an adaptive prioritization rubric that scores each inbound private deployment request on (1) data sensitivity classification, (2) network maturity (a composite probe + questionnaire score), and (3) business impact. Use the resulting score to route requests into clear lanes: Fast-track (SLA), Standard (scheduled), Deferred (self-serve remediation), and Manual Security Review. The rubric should be automatable for self-serve customers and human-review friendly for exceptions.
rationale: Aligns prioritization to risk & business value: high-sensitivity workloads on immature networks are high-risk and should get dedicated engineering intake and SRE involvement, whereas low-sensitivity workloads with mature networks can be routed to self-serve or standard onboarding. This reduces mean time to onboard for strategic customers while protecting engineering capacity and minimizing security exposure.
proposed_rubric: Score components (0-100 total): DataSensitivity 0-40, NetworkMaturity 0-40, BusinessImpact 0-20.
DataSensitivity scoring (0-40): public < internal < regulated < PHI/PII-high (map to 0/10/25/40). Include data residency constraints as +5 if strict region lock required.

NetworkMaturity scoring (0-40): composite of self-declared questionnaire (max 20) and automated probe results (max 20). Probes check: egress openness, NAT/proxy behavior, TLS termination inspection, permitted ports, and upgrade cadence (windows between upgrades).
BusinessImpact scoring (0-20): revenue exposure, SLA need, number of affected users (map small/medium/large to 0/8/15 and strategic account bonus +5).

Lane thresholds: Fast-track >= 80 (assign Dedicated intake, SRE preflight + 72h SLA), Standard 55-79 (PM-led onboarding with scheduled eng work), Manual Review 40-54 (security & legal signoff required), Deferred < 40 (self-serve remediation playbook + template engagement).

Exception rules: Any DataSensitivity == 40 (PHI) automatically triggers Manual Review regardless of numeric total. If automated probes detect blocked egress or corporate proxy mutating TLS, escalate to SRE even if overall score would be Standard.
Produce an explanation string for customers and sales in the intake UI with the numeric breakdown and next steps links.
Persist scores and probe results in onboarding DB for post-mortem and automation tuning.
acceptance_criteria: Scoring algorithm documented in Confluence with mapping table and examples for 8 representative customer profiles.
Automated preflight probe implemented as a serverless job that can be invoked from the intake form; returns a JSON-compatible status (OK/WARN/FAIL) and numeric sub-scores.
Intake UI shows the computed lane and the human-readable rationale to the customer and AE, with an option to request manual review.
Routing automation sends Fast-track requests to Dedicated onboarding queue (SRE + Eng), Standard to PM-run queue, and Deferred to self-serve docs with automated follow-up emails.
Telemetry: dashboard with rate of requests per lane, average time-to-first-response per lane, and false-positive/negative manual-review overrides tracked for 3 weeks after launch.
implementation_plan: Week 1: Finalize rubric and edge-case rules with Security, SRE, Sales Engineering. Owner: PM (Diego).
Week 2: Build and ship intake form changes + questionnaire. Owner: FE (Arielle Chen) + PM review.
Week 3: Implement automated probe (serverless job) and scoring function in onboarding service. Owner: ENG (SRE rotation: Priya Nair).
Week 4: Hook routing automation to queues (Zendesk/Linear/Oncall). Owner: Platform Eng + Ops.
Week 5: Internal dogfood with 5 active customer requests; collect feedback and tune thresholds. Owner: PM + SRE.
Week 6: Launch soft beta; monitor telemetry and prepare runbook for Manual Review collisions. Owner: PM + Support.
Post-launch: Tuning sprint (2 weeks) to adjust weights based on observed outcomes.
risks: Automated probes may produce false negatives on complex corporate proxy stacks causing under-prioritization.
Customers may perceive the numeric score as opaque or unfair; messaging must provide clear remediation steps and appeals path.
Too aggressive Fast-track thresholds could overload dedicated engineering capacity; require backstop quota for fast-track per quarter.
Legal/compliance edge cases (cross-border data residency) may need longer manual timelines than the rubric implies.
